name: Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi energy function E = (Gamma^2 - 1)/2; E > 0 is the unbound (hyperbolic) shell; FRW criterion k < 0

source.located: Classic: Lemaitre 1933 (Ann. Soc. Sci. Bruxelles A53, 51), Tolman 1934 (PNAS 20, 169), Bondi 1947 (MNRAS 107, 410) -- all pre-arXiv, NAMED-NOT-READ. Read via exact restatements: Hellaby arXiv:0910.0350 eqs (2.1),(2.5),(2.9)-(2.11),(2.31)-(2.32) [LT metric with f = 2E, evolution equation, hyperbolic/parabolic/elliptic, RW limit f = -k r^2]; Enqvist arXiv:0709.2044 eqs (2.9),(2.12) [k(r) form, k(r) -> k r^2]; Escriva arXiv:2504.05813 eqs (2.3),(2.5) [Gamma = D_r R, Gamma^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2M/R, the owner's own citation]; Hayward gr-qc/9408002 eq (27) [Misner-Sharp form, the owner's other citation]; Lasky & Lun gr-qc/0606055 eqs (40),(42) and Sec. IV [E with pressure; 'E positive, negative, zero correspond to unbound, bound, marginally bound']; Le Delliou, Mena & Mimoso arXiv:0911.0241 eq (15), Fig. 1 [escape criterion with Lambda].
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 0910.0350, 0709.2044, 2504.05813, gr-qc/9408002, gr-qc/0606055, 0911.0241 (six calls, page text returned and quoted below)

published_statement: Hellaby 0910.0350 (2.1): ds^2 = -dt^2 + (R')^2/(1+f) dr^2 + R^2 dOmega^2; 'The matter is a pressure-free perfect fluid ... comoving'; (2.5): Rdot^2 = 2M/R + f + Lambda R^2/3; 'f(r) also plays the role of twice the local energy per unit mass of the dust particles, so it's often written f(r) = 2E(r)'; (2.9)-(2.11): 'Lambda = 0, f > 0 ... f = 0 ... f < 0 ... for hyperbolic, parabolic, and elliptic evolution respectively'; (2.32): RW special case 'f = -k r^2'. Escriva 2504.05813 (2.3),(2.5): Gamma = (1/B) dR/dr = D_r R; Gamma = sqrt(1 + U^2 - 2M/R), 'where Gamma is called the generalised Lorentz factor', for a perfect fluid (p + rho) in comoving gauge. Lasky & Lun gr-qc/0606055 Sec. IV: 'the function E, is simply the energy function of the standard LTB model. In this way, the cases of E being positive, negative or equivalently zero correspond to unbound, bound and marginally bound models respectively' -- stated AT the reduction 'as the pressure vanishes'; their eq (42) r' dE/dT = 2 (1+E)/(rho+P) P' alpha sqrt(2M/r + E) makes E time-dependent when P' != 0. Le Delliou et al. 0911.0241 eq (15) with Lambda: rdot^2 = 2M/r + Lambda r^2/3 + E; 'the fate of the shell is either to remain bound (E < E_lim) or to escape and cosmologically expand (E > E_lim)', E_lim = -(3M)^{2/3} Lambda^{1/3}.
published_hypotheses: dust: pressure-free perfect fluid T^ab = rho u^a u^b (Hellaby 2.3) -- E(r) is a conserved per-shell label only then (Lasky-Lun eq 42)

Lambda = 0 for the hyperbolic/parabolic/elliptic classification by the sign of f (Hellaby 2.9-2.11 are stated 'Lambda = 0'); Lambda = 0 and M > 0 for 'E > 0 <=> unbound' (Le Delliou eq 15 gives E_lim < 0 when Lambda > 0)
RW limit: f = -k r^2, M = M_3 r^3, a' = 0 (Hellaby 2.31-2.32)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED dust (p = 0): driven.py:214-217 and drivensource.py:183-186 attach the LTB label to the general perfect-fluid Misner-Sharp identity (Escriva 2.5, any p). Consequence, computed (V6a-c): Gamma^2 - 1 = 2E remains an identity instant by instant, but E is not a conserved shell label when P' != 0 (Lasky-Lun eq 42), so 'THE CONFIGURATION IS UNBOUND' (drivensource.py:186) is an instantaneous statement, not a fate. drivensource.py's own extraction record already flags this restriction as unnamed.

DROPPED Lambda = 0: Lambda is named nowhere in driven.py (grep 'Lambda' hits only the metric function Lambda(t,r)); the tree's m is the general Misner-Sharp mass, into which any Lambda enters as Lambda R^3/6 (V2b). With Lambda > 0 a dust shell with E_lim < E < 0 escapes to infinity (Le Delliou eq 15; computed V5c: M = 1, Lambda = 0.1, E = -0.4827, rdot^2 > 0 at every r in (0,1000]) while Gamma^2 = 1 + 2E < 1, i.e. NOT 'contracting' in driven.py's sense. So 'contraction <=> unbound' (driven.py:215, drivensource.py:186) is a Lambda = 0 statement. Site: driven.py:214-217, 513-514; drivensource.py:183-186.

ADDED (terminology, not a hypothesis): the tree's 'contraction' is Gamma > 1 = proper radial length shorter than the areal increment (driven.py:384-387). In LTB the E > 0 'hyperbolic' shells are exactly the ones that never recollapse (V4a). The tree's sentence 'This is why open FRW contracts and flat FRW does not' (driven.py:216-217) is exact for Gamma > 1 (V3) but reads, in LTB vocabulary, as the opposite of what 'contracts' means there. A discrepancy of words, recorded; not a refutation.

KEPT: spherical symmetry (driven.py section 7 SCOPE 'spherically symmetric only'); comoving gauge (Escriva's Gamma is the comoving-gauge D_r R, and the tree's Gamma = e^{-Lambda} R' is the same object); 1 + 2E > 0 is enforced by driven.gamma() raising on Gamma^2 < 0.

NOT DRIFTED: the FRW criterion 'k < 0' as a statement about Gamma > 1 is exact for any FRW fluid, dust or not (V3: Gamma^2 = 1 - k r^2 needs only R = a r and g_rr = a^2/(1 - k r^2)); the tree does not restrict it to dust and need not.

CONVENTION (no drift): Hellaby writes 1 + f = 1 + 2E; Lasky-Lun write 1 + E_LL with E_LL = f; the tree uses Hellaby's 1 + 2E (driven.py:599). A reader comparing with Lasky-Lun sees a factor 2 that is notation (V7).

later_literature.ref: Hayward, gr-qc/9408002, PRD 53 (1996) 1938, eq (27) and Sec. IV
later_literature.what: Restates Misner-Sharp 1964 in the form 1 - 2E_MS/r = e^{-lambda} r'^2 - rdot^2 (the E there is the Misner-Sharp ENERGY, the tree's m, not the LTB E -- two different E's; the tree keeps them apart by writing m). Confirms the identity the LTB reading is built on. Also states 'in the absence of pressure, E is conserved' (his (32b)) for the Misner-Sharp energy -- the same dust condition.

Gamma = D_r R, Gamma^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2M/R, 'generalised Lorentz factor, which includes the gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy per unit mass' -- for a general perfect fluid p = w rho in comoving gauge; the Gamma^2 - 1 = 2E reading is not stated there, and Gamma takes NEGATIVE values in type-II throats (R' < 0), a regime where 'Gamma > 1' and 'E > 0' come apart in sign of Gamma (E > 0 iff |Gamma| > 1).

Generalised LTB with pressure: the metric keeps g_RR = r'^2/(1+E) so the identity survives, but E(T,R) evolves via P' -- the bound/unbound label is conserved only for dust. States the E > 0 unbound / E < 0 bound / E = 0 marginal classification explicitly at the dust reduction.

later_literature.ref: Le Delliou, Mena & Mimoso, arXiv:0911.0241 (2009), eq (15), Fig. 1; the PRD version Mimoso, Le Delliou & Mena arXiv:0910.5755
later_literature.what: With Lambda > 0 a dust shell escapes iff E > E_lim = -(3M)^{2/3} Lambda^{1/3} < 0, so E > 0 is no longer necessary for unboundedness; a shell separating collapse from expansion 'must be located in an elliptic (E < 0) region'. 0911.0241 READ; 0910.5755 NAMED-NOT-READ (restated by the proceedings).

The LT metric, f = 2E, the three evolution types at Lambda = 0, the RW limit f = -k r^2; also 'When Lambda != 0 there is a very complicated solution in terms of elliptic integrals' -- the sign-of-f classification is stated only for Lambda = 0.
LTB in k(r) form, g_rr = A'^2/(1 - k(r)), first integral Adot^2/A^2 = F/A^3 + 8piG rho_Lambda/3 - k/A^2, FRW limit k(r) -> k r^2 -- i.e. 2E = -k(r), and the Lambda term kept explicitly.

lacked_data: The result is a definition plus an algebraic identity, and no datum enters it (V1-V3 are symbolic with residual 0), so the identity Gamma^2 - 1 = 2E could not have been changed by data the 1933/1934/1947 authors lacked. The one later datum that touches the RESULT AS THE TREE USES IT is the sign of Lambda: the E > 0 <=> unbound gloss is a Lambda = 0 (and dust) statement, and Lambda > 0 -- the standard reading of the 1998 supernova data (Enqvist 0709.2044 Sec. 1, READ) -- moves the escape threshold to E_lim < 0 (Le Delliou 0911.0241 eq 15, READ; computed V5a-c). Evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis helping the warp case: the moved datum makes E > 0 (Gamma > 1) merely sufficient for unboundedness, not necessary, so it does not widen the class of Gamma > 1 configurations and leaves driven.py's Gamma > 1 <=> 2m/R < U^2 criterion, and every ledger row, exactly where they were. Evidence FOR the hypothesis as a general matter: the classic classification was indeed written in a Lambda = 0 frame (Hellaby 2.9-2.11 as restated), and a later measurement did change its physical reading -- but towards MORE unbound shells, not towards any escape from the corridor bill. Whether Lemaitre's 1933 paper itself carried Lambda in the classification is not settled here (NAMED-NOT-READ).
grade_evidence: The statement splits into three parts. (i) Gamma^2 - 1 = 2E as an identity of the LTB metric form: STANDS -- re-derived (V1, V1b residual 0), agrees with the owner's V9 (residual 0 on a read-only run of driven.py --verify), survives Lambda (V2b) and pressure at each instant (V6a). (ii) The FRW criterion Gamma > 1 <=> k < 0: STANDS for any FRW fluid (V3, V3n). (iii) 'E > 0 is the unbound shell' / 'CONTRACTION <=> ... UNBOUND' (driven.py:214-217, 513-514; drivensource.py:183-186): holds on a SMALLER class than the tree's general perfect-fluid Misner-Sharp identity -- the source states it for dust (Hellaby 2.3; Lasky-Lun Sec. IV 'as the pressure vanishes') with Lambda = 0 (Hellaby 2.9-2.11), and both hypotheses are dropped by the owners. The Lambda drop is shown to matter by a computed counterexample (V5c: an unbound dust shell with E < 0, Gamma < 1, for Lambda = 0.1, M = 1, using the tree's own gamma_squared with the Misner-Sharp m); the dust drop is shown to matter by Lasky-Lun eq (42) (V6c: E is not conserved when P' != 0). Not WRONG: nothing the tree computes is contradicted, and no ledger row or specthm class rests on the LTB gloss; the contraction_is_unbound fixture (driven.py:398-406, 699-701) tests Gamma > 1 <=> (Gamma^2-1)/2 > 0, which is a tautology in E's own definition and passes on any data. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no number is contested. The 'open FRW contracts' wording (driven.py:216) is a discrepancy of vocabulary with LTB usage, recorded and not counted against the grade.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owners naming 'dust, Lambda = 0' as hypotheses at driven.py:214-217/513-514 and drivensource.py:183-186 (a two-line scope note; the tree's chat-67 hold means this audit records it, it does not make the edit), or a reading of Lemaitre 1933 at source showing the classification was stated with Lambda and a general escape threshold -- which would move the SOURCE, not the tree's use, and the Lambda counterexample would still stand against the tree's sentence. To WRONG: a computed case where Gamma > 1 (2m/R < U^2, m the Misner-Sharp mass) and (Gamma^2-1)/2 <= 0 -- impossible by V1, so WRONG is closed for parts (i) and (ii). To DATA-DEPENDENT: would need a numerical datum entering the conclusion; none does.
